summary_en: Mebuki Financial Group raised its full-year dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027, increasing the year-end dividend by 4 yen to 26 yen per share, bringing the total annual dividend to 48 yen from the previous forecast of 44 yen, driven by higher than expected net income of 112.0 billion yen reflecting improved funding margins from Bank of Japan rate increases.
title_en: Notice of Revision to Full-Year Earnings Forecast and Year-End Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
On November 11, 2026, Mebuki Financial Group announced a revision to its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The company raised the year-end dividend per share from 22 yen to 26 yen, an increase of 4 yen. Combined with the already-distributed interim dividend of 22 yen, the total annual dividend is now projected at 48 yen per share, up 4 yen from the previously forecast 44 yen.

The revision reflects stronger-than-expected earnings, with the company raising its full-year consolidated net income attributable to parent company shareholders to 112.0 billion yen from the prior forecast of 105.0 billion yen, a gain of 7.0 billion yen. This upward earnings revision was driven by improved funding margins. In September 2026, the Bank of Japan raised its policy interest rate, which increased yields on the company's lending portfolio and securities holdings, generating higher net interest income and securities-related income than previously anticipated.

The dividend increase aligns with the company's stated shareholder return policy of pursuing stable and sustainable per-share dividend growth through profit growth, with a target dividend payout ratio of 40% or higher by fiscal 2027. This represents a significant dividend increase compared to the prior fiscal year ending March 2026, when the company paid annual dividends of 28 yen per share (12 yen interim plus 16 yen year-end).
